newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Ciba SC shares rise as trading begins.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ciba SC shares rise as trading begins.

text.p: Shares of Ciba Specialty Holding Inc powered higher on their first day of trading on Thursday, crowning one of Europe's biggest spin-offs with solid gains against a generally weaker Swiss stock market.

Shares of Ciba SC, being spun off from phramaceuticals giant Novartis, opened at 112.75 Swiss francs ($77.51), above the 110-franc issue price set for its global stock offering. After dipping briefly, they hit a high of 118 before meeting profit-taking.
They were quoted at 114 around 1150 GMT.

"There is big demand from the Anglo-Saxon area," one Swiss dealer said, adding that British investors sought shares to balance their portfolios in line with the weightings of the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI).

Some Novartis shareholders, who sold their subscription rights to Ciba SC thinking profit-taking would push prices lower at first, were also scrambling to climb back aboard, he said, as were investors who failed to be allotted any shares.
A series of option issues on Ciba was also helping to support prices, one dealer said, adding that retail business was not very large but tended to be on the buy side.

The issue price valued the company at around 7.93 billion Swiss francs and reflected surprisingly strong demand that kept prices well above the price range of 72 to 86 first indicated last month by a bank consortium handling the deal.
The consortium had offered on Monday night to buy the rights for 90 francs. It then used the rights to allocate 3.01 million shares in the global offering.
Ciba SC Chairman Rolf Meyer told Reuters he was satisfied with demand that emerged during the rights trading period.
"We are very pleased at the interest both domestically and internationally, and obviously the good market conditions also helped," he said by telephone from Basle.
But he declined to forecast how the share price would perform. Analysts have said shares were fairly valued fundamentally at around 100 Swiss francs.

Subscription rights for Ciba SC, spun off via a one-for-one rights issue to Novartis shareholders, had closed at 103.50 francs on Tuesday. That valued shares at 113.50 francs given the 10-franc subscription charge.
The implied price/earnings ratio at that level for the rights put Ciba SC at a premium to Clariant and other specialty chemical companies in Europe.

Ciba SC had 1996 sales of more than 6.7 billion francs from additives, consumer care chemicals, polymers, pigments and textile dyes. It is the world's leader in additives, whiteners, certain polymers and pigments. It is second in textile dyes.
Meyer told Reuters he expected most of the company's stock to be owned by Swiss shareholders.

"My rough estimate would be that we may have over 50 percent Swiss shareholders, some 20 percent or thereabouts in the U.K., maybe 10 to 15 percent in the U.S. and the rest would be continental Europe and the rest of the world," he said. "But obviously that can still change."
Ciba SC planned to report first quarter results and unveil its opening balance sheet in early May. He declined to comment on business developments so far in 1997.

More than 20,000 employees will get a certificate entitling each to the market value of one share on March 1, 2000 and which can be redeemed in March 2000. "This clearly indicates to all our employees the importance of the contribution in delivering shareholder value," Meyer said in a statement. ($ = 1.454 Swiss Francs)
